findings.title: Enemy-reset ownership split between pursuit/search and status-effect/displacement is an open internal-decomposition question, not a coverage gap
findings.description: The candidate's own `unresolved_questions` array asks whether the enemy-owned restart/reset operation that returns a persistent enemy to its authored spawn region with cleared pursuit/search/status/displacement state should live entirely on `enemy-pursuit-search-foundation`, be split with `enemy-status-effect-displacement`, or be represented some other way, since no enemy code exists yet to show the real component boundary. This is legitimate and honestly disclosed uncertainty rather than a missing requirement: both `enemy-status-effect-displacement` and `enemy-pursuit-search-foundation` already carry their own owner-controlled reset entry points in their acceptance criteria, and `floor-run-restart-persistent-closure` already depends on both. Nothing required by the GDD is at risk of being silently forgotten by the graph; the only open item is exactly how the eventual C# reset call is partitioned once enemy code is written.

gdd_evidence.requirement: Every system that owns state that can persist or remain active when restart occurs must expose a reset entry point for the state it owns, and the orchestrator invokes those owned reset interfaces. Required reset participants include ... enemy pursuit/search/attack/status/displacement state.

findings.recommended_change: No graph change required now. Keep the unresolved question tagged `later_decomposition`; resolve the exact reset-call split once the enemy-pursuit-search-foundation and enemy-status-effect-displacement components exist and their real state ownership boundary is visible in code.

notes: Audit scope was restricted to Enemy Health/Defeat, Active Enemy Registry, persistent enemy bookkeeping, Frost slowdown application/restoration, forced displacement/state hand-back, defeat bookkeeping, and enemy-state reset, per the PARALLEL AUDIT SCOPE — Coverage — Enemy State directive. Enemy pursuit/detection/target-loss mechanics, Melee/Ranged archetype behavior, locked-door enemy attack, encounter admission/content authoring, and door/navigation work were read only to verify owner/consumer contracts touching this territory (e.g. active-enemy-registry <- enemy-health-damage-defeat, enemy-pursuit-search-foundation <- enemy-status-effect-displacement) and were not independently audited for their own coverage.

The candidate durably represents all three core enemy-state capabilities as distinct, non-buried top-level implementation keys under the 'enemies' feature: active-enemy-registry, enemy-health-damage-defeat, and enemy-status-effect-displacement. None of them are hidden inside a consumer (Fireball, Frost Field, Force Wave) — the audited anti-pattern of a shared capability being buried in one consumer's notes is not present here.

GDD Section 5's explicit bundling of Frost-slowdown apply/restore and forced-displacement apply/restore into 'a reusable status-effect/displacement component' is correctly honored by grouping both effect types into the single enemy-status-effect-displacement work item rather than splitting them, consistent with the audit's grouping-is-valid guidance.

Dependency direction is correct throughout: enemy-status-effect-displacement depends on enemy-pursuit-search-foundation and gameplay-navigation-locomotion (both real, currently-unfinished prerequisites per GDD Runtime Implementation text); enemy-health-damage-defeat depends on active-enemy-registry (defeat must report through the registry's own unregister interface); active-enemy-registry has no upstream dependency, matching the GDD's explicit 'does not require the exact five-room encounter layouts... to be known first' framing. No feature->feature dependency edges appear in this territory.

floor-run-restart-persistent-closure correctly lists active-enemy-registry, enemy-health-damage-defeat, and enemy-status-effect-displacement (plus enemy-pursuit-search-foundation, melee-enemy, ranged-enemy, locked-door-enemy-attack) as required reset-participant dependencies, satisfying the GDD's full persistent-restart-closure requirement for this domain.

The GDD-critical acceptance criterion that Frost Field slowdown must never suppress or slow a Ranged Enemy's attack execution (only locomotion/repositioning) is explicitly and separately stated as its own acceptance criterion and validation requirement on enemy-status-effect-displacement, matching the 'Final material convergence' explicit-representation guidance rather than leaving it evidence-only.

requirements.reference: Section 3 — Enemy health and defeat ownership
requirements.requirement: A reusable Enemy Health/Defeat capability owns each persistent enemy object's current health, damage intake, defeat transition, and restartable health/defeat state.
requirements.explanation: Represented as its own durable implementation key under the 'enemies' feature, not buried inside Fireball or another consumer.

requirements.reference: Section 3 — Enemy health and defeat ownership
requirements.requirement: Fireball and any other canon-required damage source request damage through the Enemy Health/Defeat owner-controlled interface rather than writing enemy health directly.
requirements.explanation: Captured as an explicit acceptance criterion on the owning work item, with the consumer side (Fireball) correctly depending on it rather than duplicating ownership.

requirements.reference: Section 3 — Enemy health and defeat ownership
requirements.requirement: When defeat occurs, the Enemy Health/Defeat owner reports that transition through the Active Enemy Registry owner's removal/unregister interface so the active count is updated without duplicating registry bookkeeping.
requirements.explanation: Both sides of the interface contract are represented: enemy-health-damage-defeat's acceptance criteria require calling the unregister interface, and active-enemy-registry's acceptance criteria state only a defeat-driven unregister call removes an enemy. enemy-health-damage-defeat correctly depends_on active-enemy-registry.

requirements.reference: Section 3 — Enemy health and defeat ownership; Section 2 — Floor-run restart ownership
requirements.requirement: Floor restart restores enemy health/defeat state through the enemy-owned reset entry point; the Floor Run/Restart Orchestrator does not mutate enemy-health internals directly.
requirements.explanation: enemy-health-damage-defeat exposes the reset entry point as an acceptance criterion; floor-run-restart-persistent-closure lists enemy-health-damage-defeat as a required dependency/reset participant.

requirements.reference: Section 3 — Active Enemy Registry and Encounter Admission
requirements.requirement: A shared Active Enemy Registry tracks the persistent enemy objects currently active in the run and exposes the current active count and remaining capacity under the hard limit of fifteen.
requirements.explanation: Represented as its own durable implementation key, matching the taxonomy's expectation for a required reusable runtime foundation.

requirements.reference: Section 3 — Active Enemy Registry and Encounter Admission
requirements.requirement: Enemy activation registers an enemy with the registry; defeat removes that enemy from the active count. Target loss, searching, crossing rooms, or waiting behind a locked door does not remove a surviving persistent enemy from the registry.
requirements.explanation: Directly captured as an explicit acceptance criterion and validation requirement, including the negative cases (target loss/search/room crossing/locked-door wait) that must NOT unregister an enemy.

requirements.requirement: Active Enemy Registry bookkeeping is a required reset participant invoked through the registry's own owner-controlled reset entry point during floor restart, and the post-restart count must agree with the live set of restored persistent enemies.
requirements.explanation: Captured with an unusually specific acceptance criterion requiring post-restart count/live-enemy consistency, and wired as a dependency of the persistent-closure restart item.

requirements.reference: Section 3 — Door and Pursuit Rules; Section 3 — Active Enemy Registry and Encounter Admission
requirements.requirement: Surviving enemies carry forward and combine with later encounters as the same persistent enemy objects, not new spawns, and the game never permits more than fifteen active enemies at once.
requirements.explanation: The hard fifteen-cap enforcement is an acceptance criterion on active-enemy-registry; the never-respawned persistent-object identity half of this sentence belongs to the separate enemy_behavior audit territory (enemy-pursuit-search-foundation) and is out of scope here.

requirements.requirement: A reusable status-effect/displacement component will apply Frost Field slowdown, apply enemy-owned forced displacement requests, and restore each enemy to the appropriate pursuit/search movement state afterward.
requirements.explanation: Represented as its own durable implementation key bundling both effect types exactly as the GDD describes a single reusable component, rather than splitting or burying it inside Frost Field/Force Wave.

requirements.reference: Section 2 — Spell and Enemy Interactions (Frost Field row)
requirements.requirement: Frost Field slows a Ranged Enemy's repositioning but does not stop its attacks.
requirements.explanation: Explicitly stated as its own acceptance criterion ('must never suppress, pause, or slow a Ranged Enemy's attack execution/timing') and validation requirement, satisfying the explicit-representation closure guidance rather than leaving it evidence-only.

requirements.requirement: Frost slowdown is restored (movement speed returns to normal) when the effect ends, with no permanent slowdown remaining.
requirements.explanation: Directly captured as an acceptance criterion and validation requirement.

requirements.requirement: Force Wave determines which enemies are affected and the radial knockback to request; the enemy movement system applies that displacement, preserves valid movement/navigation state, and resumes the appropriate pursuit/search state afterward.
requirements.explanation: Captured as acceptance criteria on enemy-status-effect-displacement (apply displacement, preserve navigation state, hand back to pursuit/search); Force Wave's own item correctly only owns the request side and depends on this owner-side capability.

requirements.requirement: The status-effect/displacement component consumes the pursuit/search state contract rather than defining a second enemy-state machine; that contract must therefore exist before status-effect/displacement work is treated as independently dispatchable.
requirements.explanation: Correctly represented as a real depends_on edge from enemy-status-effect-displacement to enemy-pursuit-search-foundation (both implementation-kind nodes, not a feature->feature edge), matching the GDD-stated ordering.

requirements.reference: Section 2 — Spell-local state ownership; Section 2 — Floor-run restart ownership
requirements.requirement: Enemy-side Frost slowdown application/restoration state and forced-displacement state are required reset participants; each owner exposes a reset entry point for any owned state that can still be active when a floor restart occurs.
requirements.explanation: enemy-status-effect-displacement exposes the reset entry point as an acceptance criterion; floor-run-restart-persistent-closure lists it as a required dependency/reset participant.

requirements.requirement: Required reset participants for the Floor Run/Restart Orchestrator include enemy health/defeat state, enemy pursuit/search/attack/status/displacement state, and Active Enemy Registry bookkeeping.
requirements.explanation: floor-run-restart-persistent-closure explicitly depends on all three enemy-state-domain owners as named required reset participants, satisfying full persistent-restart-closure coverage for this territory.

requirements.reference: Section 4 — Enemy Pursuit Agent role; Section 4 — Development Agent Ownership Invariants
requirements.requirement: The Enemy Pursuit Agent owns the reusable Enemy Health/Defeat capability, Frost slowdown application/restoration, forced displacement, and the shared Active Enemy Registry bookkeeping as a development-process ownership boundary.
requirements.explanation: The cross-cutting ownership-invariant rule is captured as a typed pipeline_constraint non_code_requirement, while the concrete per-capability runtime split is separately embodied as acceptance criteria on enemy-health-damage-defeat, active-enemy-registry, and enemy-status-effect-displacement, matching the split-compound-passage guidance.

requirements.reference: Section 3 — Active Enemy Registry and Encounter Admission
requirements.requirement: The registry/bookkeeping responsibility is a reusable runtime foundation and does not require the exact five-room encounter layouts, placements, or trigger authoring to be known first.
requirements.explanation: Reflected in active-enemy-registry's decomposition_reason and its lack of any dependency on room/encounter content work, correctly keeping it dispatchable independent of deferred five-room authoring.
